name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean with incumbent Jonathan Jackson renominated
Challenger Christian Maxwell's modest fundraising (~$95k) versus Jackson's ~$539k
Prediction markets price Jackson at roughly 96% to win
No general-election polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic tilt, Jackson's incumbency, and the challenger's thin war chest make an upset highly unlikely, and prediction markets price Democrats near certain. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal involving Jackson or a surge of outside spending for Maxwell could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes a flip very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 1st District, anchored on Chicago's South Side, leans heavily Democratic with a partisan advantage of about 18 points. Jonathan Jackson, first elected in 2022, is seeking re-election after securing the Democratic nomination. Republican Christian Maxwell enters the general election with modest resources, having raised roughly $95,000, while Jackson has brought in about $539,000 this cycle, though he ends the period with limited cash on hand.

No public general-election polling is available, and professional race raters have not flagged this contest as competitive. Prediction markets price Jackson's chances at roughly 96 percent. The combination of the district's strong Democratic tilt, incumbency, and the challenger's thin fundraising makes an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
